title: WPMS/3225/2019 of PALVINDER SINGH Vs VICE CHANCELLOR GOVIND BALLABH PANT UNIVERSITY OF AGRICULTURE AND TECHNOLOGY

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS

In
WPMS No. 3225 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Saurav Pandey, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Shubhang Dobhal, Advocate for the
respondents.
Though the matter is listed on an
Amendment Application, but on a consideration of
the controversy in its totality, the petitioner has
sought the following reliefs in the Writ Petition :-
"i) Issue a Writ Order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus commanding and directing the
respondents to permit the petitioner to harvest the
crop on the plot basis over the leased out land in
favour of the petitioner and to permit him to deposit
the remaining amount of license fee after harvesting
his respective crops.
ii) Issue any other order or direction this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts
and circumstances of the case."
Apart from the amended relief, which has
been sought by filing an Amendment Application
by incorporating a relief to the effect that a writ of
mandamus may be issued to respondents for
adjusting the difference of amount of the crop
harvested as sold by the petitioner and the crop
which is harvested and sold by the University and
also to conduct a high level independent inquiry
relating to the embezzlement of the harvested crop
amount.
As far as law of writ of mandamus is
concerned, it is a settle proposition of law, that a
writ of mandamus could only lie for an enforcement
of the statutory right created under law, which
could be enforced by writ jurisdiction under Article
226 of the Constitution of India, if there is an
apparent breach of any fundamental right created by
the Constitution or statutory right, created by law.

The scope of Article 226 of the Constitution
of India and writ of mandamus, cannot be stretch to
an extent to include within its the terms of the
contract, which governs the inter se relationship
between the two contracting parties.
The petitioner, herein, since have entered into
the contract for the purposes of harvesting the crops
and a licence has been executed in their favour as
per the covenant of the agreement dated 12th May,
2019, the said contract in its Clause 36, which is
extracted hereunder, provides that in an eventuality,
if there arises any dispute between the contracting
parties, the same would be adjudicated through an
Arbitrator. Clause 36 reads as under :-

In view of the aforesaid Clause 36 of the
Contract, no writ of mandamus, particularly of the
nature of relief sought, would be maintainable.
Hence, the Writ Petition is dismissed. All
contentions, which have been raised by the
petitioner in the present Writ Petition are left open
to be agitated by the petitioner before the
Arbitrator.
